svg.title: The Law-Firm MSO Blueprint
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-law-firm-mso-architecture; chapter number: 11; title: The Law-Firm MSO Blueprint; subtitle: Non-lawyer operations spun out, legal judgment kept inside the firm; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: MSO (Delaware LLC); headcount: All non-lawyer staff, plus equipment, IP and founder likeness; focus: Leased back for a fixed monthly or cost-plus fee with 10-15% markups, validated by a third-party fairness opinion; spokes: role: Law firm; type: Licensed practice; kpi: Keeps lawyers, engagement letters, trust accounts, hiring, case selection and settlement; mind the UnitedLex improper-control finding; role: Fairness opinion provider; type: Third-party validator; kpi: Fee re-priced forward-looking only, on a roughly annual cadence; role: PE buyer; type: Equity capital; kpi: Buy in at 5x to roll up PI firms at 35% margins; law firms trade at 4-8x versus about 15x for accounting; role: Litigation funder; type: Portfolio capital; kpi: Burford funds 6-8% of reviewed cases at mid-20s IRRs; 39 funders committed $2.8B in 2025; caption: Spin operations into the MSO, lease them back, and keep every legal decision with the lawyers.; assumptions note: MSO fees must never be a percentage of profits or revenue. Practitioners disagree on mass-tort cash-flow unpredictability and true portfolio diversification.; note: Sources: Holland & Knight's Trisha Rich and Josh Port on Confido Legal (5TjsKzLtyc4), Joe Prencipe, Chris Bogart on TALKSONLAW (1kAfGIkF10g), The National Law Review (9teRv9eFpEc), Jon and Marc (U2xFBBUm_IU).

text.title: Assumptions: MSO fees must never be a percentage of profits or revenue. Practitioners disagree on mass-tort cash-flow unpredictability and true portfolio diversification.
